newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopian court told Marxists sold corpses.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopian court told Marxists sold corpses.

text.p: A witness in the trial of Ethiopia's former Marxist leaders on Tuesday told how the military junta sold the bodies of its murdered victims back to their families.
The witness, who under court rules cannot be named, spent four years in prison as a government opponent in the 1970s and is now a member of Ethiopia's parliament.
The courtroom was filled with sobs from traumatised relatives as he told of the selling of bodies and graphically described the way he was tortured.

"I only know that the Dergue regime was selling dead bodies and parents were buying back the remains of their loved ones," the witness said when asked if he could give the names of those whose bodies had been sold.

Death squads in a terror campaign in 1977 and 1978 hunted down thousands of students from rival Marxist groups and other opposition organisations on behalf of the military junta, known as the "Dergue".

The government has charged more than 1,200 people suspected of involvement in the "Red Terror" campaign during the 17-year Marxist rule of dictator Mengistu Haile Mariam. They have yet to appear in court.
Only 46 out of 71 former Dergue officials accused of genocide and crimes against humanity are on trial, the 25 others including Mengistu are being tried in absentia.
All 71 could be sentenced to death if found guilty. Mengistu ruled from 1977 until May 1991 when he fled the country shortly before rebels entered the capital and set up a new administration.
For over two hours on Tuesday the witness was cross-examined by scathing defence lawyers who tried to undermine his credibility.
They were joined by Major Melaku Tefera, one of the most senior of the accused, who has dismissed his lawyer to conduct his own defence.
The witness described how he had been starved in a special prison for those the junta believed were destined to die.
"Within three months in the special Dergue prison I was redcued to a mere walking skeleton," he said.
The trial was adjourned until February 18.
